data_points.quote: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology notified the 'Scheme for Setting up of Display Fabs in India' on 21 December 2021. ... could receive fiscal support of up to 50 per cent of project cost, capped at ₹12,000 crore ... minimum capital investment of ₹10,000 crore and a minimum revenue threshold of ₹7,500 crore in any of the three years before applying.

The scheme allowed a maximum of two beneficiaries, ran for a notional six-year tenure, was implemented through the newly created India Semiconductor Mission as nodal agency, and required Union Cabinet approval of any selected applicant.
Foxconn formally withdrew from its roughly $19.5 billion joint venture with Vedanta on 10-11 July 2023
The Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0 on 15 July 2026, an outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore

support for silicon-based semiconductor fabs was cut from 50 per cent to 40 per cent of project cost; support for compound semiconductor fabs and display fabs together was cut to up to 35 per cent — down from the uniform 50 per cent the original 2021 scheme offered

a Generation-6-or-above OLED fab now needs a minimum ₹5,000 crore in revenue rather than the original ₹7,500 crore
an entirely new, much smaller Micro-LED sub-category was created, with a minimum investment of just ₹1,500 crore and revenue of ₹600 crore
